name: Taiwan Taoyuan International Airport
before:
Taiwan's busiest and largest airport, at Dayuan in Taoyuan about 40 km west of Taipei. It handled a record 46.5 million passengers in 2018, making it eleventh busiest in the world for international passengers and eighth for international freight.

There are two airports serving Taipei and the difference matters. Taoyuan handles the international traffic. Taipei Songshan sits inside the city limits and now mainly handles charter, intra-island and limited international flights, so it is far more convenient but far less useful for a long haul itinerary.

Two terminals are linked by short people movers, and the Taoyuan Airport MRT connects them underground and runs into the city. A third terminal is under construction and a fourth is planned, though those plans may be halted.

It is the main international hub for China Airlines, EVA Air and Starlux, and a hub for Mandarin Airlines, Uni Air and Tigerair Taiwan.

The airport opened in 1979 as Chiang Kai-shek International Airport and was renamed in 2006, so the old name still appears in older material.
after:
Taiwan's main international airport, in Taoyuan about 40 km west of Taipei. It handled 47.8 million passengers in 2025.

There are two airports serving Taipei and the difference matters. Taipei Songshan sits inside the city but flies only within Taiwan and to Tokyo, Seoul and mainland China, so long haul means Taoyuan.

The Taoyuan Airport MRT stops at both terminals and runs into Taipei Main Station. Since 1 July 2026 the Skytrain between them runs only airside, so passengers changing terminals before security take the free 24-hour shuttle bus or the MRT. A third terminal is due to be finished by the end of 2027.

China Airlines, EVA Air and Starlux all fly from here, as do Mandarin Airlines, Uni Air and Tigerair Taiwan.

The airport opened in 1979 as Chiang Kai-shek International Airport and was renamed in 2006, so the old name still appears in older material.

claims.claim: Taiwan's main international airport
claims.note: Was 'Taiwan's busiest and largest airport'. The national traffic table that would rank it (the Civil Aeronautics Administration's statistics) could not be reached: caa.gov.tw did not connect. So the claim is softened to what CNA and Taiwan News say: CNA quotes the transport minister calling Terminal 3 an important project for Taiwan's national gateway (國門), and Taiwan News calls it 'Taiwan main airport'. For scale: 47.8 million passengers in 2025 (CNA) against just under 7 million at Kaohsiung (the Kaohsiung airport's own monthly table, see the KHH ledger).

claims.claim: 47.8 million passengers in 2025
claims.note: Was 'a record 46.5 million passengers in 2018'. CNA reports the operator's release: 47.80 million in 2025 (ROC year 114), up 6 per cent on 44.92 million in 2024 and 98 per cent of the 2019 figure, so 2025 was not a record and 'record' goes. Wikipedia's infobox, citing the Civil Aeronautics Administration, gives 47,795,969. The operator's own site (taoyuan-airport.com) answered with a Cloudflare check and was not tried again.

claims.claim: Songshan flies only within Taiwan and to Tokyo, Seoul and mainland China
claims.inAfter: flies only within Taiwan and to Tokyo, Seoul and mainland China
claims.note: Was 'now mainly handles charter, intra-island and limited international flights'. MOTC's Transport Data eXchange schedule for flights leaving TSA (23 September to 23 October 2026, updated 24 September Taiwan time) lists every international route: Tokyo Haneda (HND), Seoul Gimpo (GMP) and seven airports in mainland China (Shanghai Hongqiao SHA and Pudong PVG, Chongqing CKG, Chengdu CTU, Fuzhou FOC, Wuhan WUH, Xiamen XMN). The Tourism Administration lists the domestic ones (Hualien, Taitung, Penghu, Kinmen, Nangan, Beigan). No charter programme was seen, so 'charter' goes, and 'mainly' goes because no source splits Songshan's traffic.

claims.claim: since 1 July 2026 the Skytrain between the terminals runs only airside
claims.inAfter: Since 1 July 2026 the Skytrain between them runs only airside
claims.note: Was 'Two terminals are linked by short people movers'. The landside (before security) Skytrain between Terminals 1 and 2 stopped on 1 July 2026 for Terminal 3 works; the airside one still runs, so transfer passengers are unaffected. CNA reports the operator's release of 30 June; Taiwan News's report of 12 June cites Liberty Times and UDN, so the two are independent accounts. The operator's own Skytrain page (taoyuan-airport.com) is behind a Cloudflare check.

quote: 配合第三航廈工程，第一、第二航廈管制區外航廈電車7月1日起停止服務

Taiwan Taoyuan International Airport will suspend its landside Skytrain service linking Terminal 1 and 2 from July 1 due to Terminal 3 connection work.
The company said that while landside inter-terminal service will cease in July, Skytrain operations within the airside will continue.
The Skytrain airside post-security trains are still operating after July 1.
